title: LinkedIn now has a ‘Seems like AI slop’ button, and yes, it really says slop

content_html:
LinkedIn has a name for the vaguely inspirational, AI-written posts clogging its feed, and now it has a button for them. The professional network has quietly added a “Seems like AI slop” option to its post menu, letting users flag content they think a machine wrote, 404 Media reported.

The button sits under the three-dot menu at the top of any post. Click it, and LinkedIn responds: “Thanks for letting us know. Your feedback helps improve the feed.” It then hides the post. 404 Media said it took about six seconds of scrolling to find a candidate, flagged by the spacing, emoji, bullet-point takeaways and “X is not Y” phrasing.

The wording is what stands out. The button does not say “this looks AI-generated.” It says “slop,” a blunt piece of internet slang for low-effort machine output, now baked into the interface of a Microsoft-owned platform.

Why LinkedIn is doing this

The move follows the platform’s May crackdown on generic AI posts, which suppressed slop from recommendations rather than removing it. The new button turns detection into a crowd-sourced signal. Every flag helps train LinkedIn’s own models to spot the stuff.

Hari Srinivasan, LinkedIn’s chief product officer, confirmed as much in a post after the report. “AI slop is a top priority for all of us,” he wrote. The company is “ramping up a series of new and improved classifiers” to identify slop, and letting members flag posts to help “tune our models and make better feeds.”

He added a telling caveat. “AI and slop are not the same thing,” Srinivasan wrote. Many people refine their thoughts with AI, so LinkedIn will test a private nudge in a poster’s analytics when their writing “may have come off as inauthentic.” It is also replacing its “enhance your post” feature with a proofreader that does not change a user’s voice.

The scale of the problem

The numbers explain the urgency. Earlier this month, 404 Media reported that the detection service Pangram estimated 41 per cent of long-form LinkedIn posts, and 30 per cent of short ones, are likely AI-generated. Search “LinkedIn AI” and you find countless guides, some hosted on LinkedIn itself, teaching people to automate their posts.

The irony is doing a lot of work here. LinkedIn offers its own AI writing assistant that drafts profiles and posts for Premium subscribers. Its parent, Microsoft, is one of OpenAI’s biggest backers. The company is, in effect, selling the hose and the mop at once.

A wider fight against slop

LinkedIn is not alone. The preprint server arXiv now bans researchers who submit AI-riddled papers, and platforms have tightened rules on mass-produced AI channels. The pressure reflects a web where bots now outnumber humans in traffic terms.

Whether a report button moves the needle is another matter. Slop is, as Srinivasan admitted, hard to define, and the definition keeps shifting. But asking users to name it, out loud, is a small admission that the feed has a problem. It also shows that proving something is human is becoming its own kind of work.

content_html_zh:
LinkedIn 为那些堵塞其提要的、模糊的鼓舞人心的人工智能撰写的帖子起了一个名字，现在它还为这些帖子提供了一个按钮。 据 404 Media 报道，该专业网络已悄然在其帖子菜单中添加了“看起来像 AI slop”选项，让用户可以标记他们认为是机器编写的内容。

该按钮位于任何帖子顶部的三点菜单下方。 点击它，LinkedIn 就会回复：“感谢您告知我们。 您的反馈有助于改进提要。” 然后它隐藏该帖子。 404 Media 表示，滚动大约六秒钟才能找到候选人，并通过空格、表情符号、要点要点和“X 不是 Y”的措辞进行标记。

措辞才是最突出的。 该按钮并没有说“这看起来是人工智能生成的”。 它说的是“slop”，这是一个直白的互联网俚语，表示轻松的机器输出，现在已经融入了微软自有平台的界面中。

LinkedIn 为何这么做

在此之前，该平台于 5 月份对通用人工智能帖子进行了打击，该帖子压制了推荐中的内容，而不是删除它。 新按钮将检测转变为众包信号。 每个标志都有助于训练 LinkedIn 自己的模型来发现这些东西。

LinkedIn 首席产品官 Hari Srinivasan 在报告发布后的一篇帖子中证实了这一点。 “人工智能问题是我们所有人的首要任务，”他写道。 该公司正在“推出一系列新的和改进的分类器”来识别垃圾，并让会员标记帖子以帮助“调整我们的模型并提供更好的信息”。

他添加了一个有说服力的警告。 “人工智能和 slop 不是一回事，”斯里尼瓦桑写道。 许多人通过人工智能完善自己的想法，因此当发帖者的写作“可能被认为不真实”时，LinkedIn 会在发帖者的分析中测试私人推动。 它还用不会改变用户声音的校对器取代了“增强你的帖子”功能。

问题的规模

这些数字说明了紧迫性。 本月早些时候，404 Media 报道称，检测服务 Pangram 估计，LinkedIn 41% 的长帖子和 30% 的短帖子很可能是人工智能生成的。 搜索“LinkedIn AI”，你会发现无数指南，其中一些托管在 LinkedIn 本身上，教人们如何自动化发布帖子。

具有讽刺意味的是，这里做了很多工作。 LinkedIn 提供自己的人工智能写作助手，可以为高级订阅者起草个人资料和帖子。 其母公司微软是 OpenAI 最大的支持者之一。 事实上，该公司同时销售软管和拖把。

更广泛地打击污水排放

LinkedIn 并不孤单。 预印本服务器 arXiv 现在禁止研究人员提交存在人工智能问题的论文，平台也收紧了对大规模生产的人工智能渠道的规则。 这种压力反映了网络中机器人的流量现在超过了人类。

报告按钮是否能起到作用是另一回事。 正如斯里尼瓦桑承认的那样，污水很难定义，而且定义一直在变化。 但要求用户大声说出它的名字，就等于承认该提要有问题。 它还表明，证明某物是人类正在成为一种独特的工作。
